dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. Good afternoon.

Good afternoon, thank you for taking my call. Um, I think I pressed the wrong option on your menu. I pressed the one for water billing, because I thought that was for the water, the drains, but a recording started talking about meter readings. So thank you, I hope I am in the right place now.
That's an easy mix-up. Water billing is a different line. If it's a drain or a street issue, you're in the right spot. What's going on?
Thank you, I appreciate that. It is a storm drain, in front of my mother's house. The address is 95 Bellevue Avenue, in the Bellevue area. I am calling for her, my name is Nadia Mensah. Thank you.
Okay, Nadia, 95 Bellevue. What's the drain doing?

Well, since last weekend's nor'easter, the Saturday into Sunday storm, it has been gurgling. Water is sitting up around it, and it is still there on a Wednesday, three days after. And there is a smell coming up from it. A sewer smell. Thank you for listening, I do not want to be rude, but this is not the first time we have had a problem with it.

No, you're not being rude at all. Gurgling and a sewer smell, that tells me it's likely backed up or something's blocked down the line. Is the water actually coming up out of the grate, or is it pooling around it?

Both, I think. It pools, and when a car goes through you can hear it bubbling [pause] sorry, a truck just went by. Yes, it bubbles up in the grate. My mother says it was like this after the last big rain too, and nobody came. Thank you.
Okay. And is it blocking the road, or is it mostly at the curb?

At the curb, mostly, but it spreads out into the road and onto the edge of her lawn. And there are children who walk that way to the bus, and people with dogs, they walk right along the edge by the water. I am worried someone will step in it, with that smell, it cannot be clean. Thank you for asking.
That's a fair concern, I'd keep kids and dogs out of it. I'll flag that in the report.
Thank you. I would like to ask, please, when did your crews last come by to this drain? My mother thinks it has been more than a year, but she is not certain. Thank you.
Let me pull up the address and see what's logged. Bear with me a second.
Of course. Thank you, take your time.

Okay, I'm looking at the Bellevue Avenue records. I'm not seeing a cleaning logged right at that grate recently. Now, I don't have a full maintenance history on my screen, just the service requests, so I'll put the question in to the drain crew supervisor and ask for their last visit.

I see. So nothing recent is recorded. I am sorry, but that is frustrating to hear, because we have waited, and my mother is elderly and she should not have to keep worrying about this. Thank you for being honest with me.

I understand. You're not wrong to be frustrated if it keeps happening. Let me get this request in properly so it gets in front of the right people. Is the grate right at the curb in front of 95, or down toward a corner?
It is right in front of 95, at the curb. Not at the corner. Thank you.
Good. And you said the water's still sitting there three days later, with the sewer odor, and it's bubbling when vehicles pass?
Yes, exactly. Thank you for repeating it. And it has been since Sunday that it hasn't gone down.

Got it. After a storm like that, the crews are stacked up with calls, but a backed-up drain with a sewer smell goes near the top of the pile. I'll mark it that way. Do you want a call back when it's been scheduled?
Yes, please, that would be very kind. Thank you. Should I give you my number?
Please. Go ahead.
It is 401-555-0170. Thank you.
401-555-0170, and that's Nadia. Right?
Yes, Nadia Mensah. M-E-N-S-A-H. Thank you.

Got it. Now, if the water starts getting into the house or the yard floods more, call us right back. And if it ever feels like an emergency, with the smell strong inside, call the main emergency line.
Thank you, I will tell my mother. Is it possible that the smell means something is wrong with the sewer and not just the drain? I do not know the difference, I am sorry.

It can be either, honestly. Storm drains and sewer lines can both get overwhelmed in a big storm. The crew will look at it and sort out which it is. I'll put the sewer odor in the notes so they bring the right people.
Thank you very much. That is helpful. And please, could you tell me roughly when someone might come? I know you cannot promise. Thank you.
I'd say within the next several days, maybe sooner since it's flagged. If you haven't heard from anyone by early next week, call back and mention this request.
Early next week. Thank you. Do I need a reference number, so that I can say which one it is?
Good idea. Hang on, it's generating. Okay, I'll give it to you slowly. Have something to write with?
Yes, I have a pen. Thank you.
PW260225-14. Did I say that correctly? Thank you.
You did. That's tied to 95 Bellevue Avenue, drain backing up with odor.

Thank you. I am sorry to take your time, but one more thing. If the water goes down by itself, should we still expect someone to come? Because last time it went down and then nobody came, and then it happened again.
Yes, the request stays open. Even if the water drops, the drain needs to be checked and cleaned, otherwise it'll just do it again with the next good rain.
Thank you, that is what I hoped you would say. My mother will be relieved, a little. Thank you, Denise, you have been very kind.
You're welcome, Nadia. Tell your mom we've got it on the list. Take care.
I will. Thank you again, and have a good afternoon. Goodbye.
You too. Bye now.
